item.group_name: Short video from a picture or text
item.title: Lake Clouds and Water Moving

turns.text: Turn this lake photo into an 8-second silent video. Let the clouds drift slowly and little ripples move across the water. Keep the mountains and trees still, same wide framing and evening light. No camera movement.

item.tests: Tests selective landscape animation of both clouds and water while preserving stationary landforms, framing and lighting.

answer_sheet.Moving elements: Slowly drifting clouds and gentle water ripples; cloud direction is your call.
answer_sheet.Stationary elements: Keep the mountains, shoreline and trees still, with no camera movement.
answer_sheet.Style and mood: Photorealistic and calm, retaining the original early-evening light.

must_haves: The mountain lake, pine trees and composition match the attached photograph.
Clouds visibly drift slowly rather than remaining frozen.
Gentle moving ripples are visible on the lake, without turning it into rough surf.
Mountains, shoreline and trees stay fixed without warping or shifting.
The camera remains stationary and the early-evening lighting stays consistent.
The output is a silent the photo's own shape (5:3) video lasting approximately 8 seconds.
changed: 2026-11-01: test fix from the careful review (F30b: the user left the length open; D18c: the photo is 5:3, not 16:9)

turns.text: Turn this lake pic into an 8-second silent video, with clouds drifting slowly and little ripples moving across the water. Keep the mountains and trees still, preserve the same wide framing and evening light, and don’t add any camera movement. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so please tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?
turns.agent:
**I haven’t started a generation or spent any credits.**

Your photo can be animated directly—no paid image-editing step is needed. The intended result would be silent, with a locked camera, slow cloud drift and subtle water ripples, preserving the mountains, trees, framing and evening light.

**Cost caveat:** the tools available here don’t expose your balance or a live price quote for direct image-to-video. The documented 480p *production* rate is **24 credits per second**, which gives these budgeting estimates—not confirmed prices for this particular job:

| Option | Estimated credits |
|---|---:|
| 8 seconds at 480p | 192 |
| 5 seconds at 480p | 120 |
| 3 seconds at 480p | 72 |

A **3-second silent preview at 480p** would be the lower-risk starting point. **480p is the lowest supported resolution** for the available free-plan video models; making it shorter is the clearest way to reduce spending. Being on the free plan doesn’t make generation credit-free.

Since you asked for the cost first, I’ll hold off. For an exact amount, check the image-to-video price displayed in Magic Hour before authorizing a run.
